rejected.title: Recommending a course of action
card: A recommendation is a clear choice of the best option from the ones being considered. It states the choice plainly.
It explains why that option beats the others. To do this, it judges each option against criteria, such as cost, fairness or effect on the environment.
It says what the option will cost. A cost includes money and also what is given up, such as time or another use of the funds.
It says who will be affected, such as customers, workers or the community. Some may gain while others lose.
rejected.remember: Name the best option, give reasons using criteria, and state the cost and who is affected.

a.q: A school can spend its grant on a new oval or a new library. Which sentence is a full recommendation?
opts: Build the library: it helps more students but costs the oval
Build the library, because libraries are good things
The oval and the library each have some real strengths
Most students would probably like a new library more
a.why: The sentence about helping more students names an option, gives a reason on a criterion, says who gains and states what is given up: the oval. Saying libraries are good things gives only a vague reason and no cost. The other two sentences do not choose an option.
a.clue: A recommendation chooses, reasons and counts the cost.

b.q: Sam recommends that a Darwin café switch to reusable cups. He says it beats the other options because it cuts waste. What is still missing?
opts: The cost of the switch and who it will affect
A statement of which option he chose
A reason why the option is better
A list of options that he rejected
b.why: Sam has named his option and given a reason about waste. He has not said what the switch will cost or who it will affect, such as customers and staff. He has already compared it with the other options, so a list of rejected options is not the missing part.
b.clue: Check each part of a recommendation against what Sam said.
